title: boopis provider catalogue
description: The shape of apps/shared/data/providers.json (ADR-0039). The Rust reader (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/providers) refuses a field this schema does not name, and the TypeScript reader (apps/desktop/ui/src/data/providers.ts) types the same fields; the tests of both check the file's structure and its examples.

wayId.description: `<entry id>.<name>`, unique in the file. A custom endpoint the user adds is `custom.<slug>` and is not in this file.

engineSlug.description: A provider slug exactly as the engine spells it.

lab.description: Whose models these are, for the lab's mark; equal to `id` unless a host serves another lab's models.

label.description: What the row is called, in boopis's words.

summary.description: One line: what the lab unlocks.

rank.description: The research ranking (ADR-0039); ties share a number. Entries are listed by rank, then in file order.

shown.description: `default`: listed in setup and Settings. `more`: under More providers (search still finds it).

keywords.description: Extra words search matches (model families, old names).

label.description: The way's name in boopis's words (no engine names).

engine.description: `model.provider`, and the part before the slash in a ladder tier. Null when boopis writes a `providers.<slug>` entry instead.

slug.description: For `config: endpoint`: the name of the `providers.<slug>` entry (fixed for a runtime on this computer, derived for a custom endpoint).

config.description: `builtin`: the engine knows the slug; setup writes only the key wiring (and a base URL when it differs). `external`: a sign-in someone else owns (claude.rs, chatgpt/). `endpoint`: boopis writes `providers.<slug>` (base_url, key_env, api_mode, models, discover_models).

hidden.description: Never listed, not even by search, and its engine slug is left out of the model picker too.

offered_when.description: `signin_unused`: the way is shown only when the entry's other sign-in is not possible or not in use (xAI: driving the user's own grok program).

region.description: A regional twin of another way; listed under it, not beside it.

slug_spike.description: A `spikes` id that settled this way's slug.

api_mode.description: How the engine talks to it (informational for `builtin`, written for `endpoint`).

frontier.description: `by_name`: a model of this route is frontier when its name is in frontier-models.json. `never`: no model of it is, ever (fail closed).

engine_source.description: Where in the engine's source (at `engine.version`) the slug and the variables were read.

vars.description: The variables the engine reads a key from, in its order. A key found under one of them by name counts as in place.

wire_var.description: The variable boopis binds to the keychain secret. One of `vars`; null for an endpoint, whose key goes by a generated name.

url.description: Where a person makes a key.

required.description: False: works without a key (a server on this computer).

refuse_prefixes.description: A key that starts with one of these is turned down with `hx.provider.key_invalid` (a plan key that is not for boopis).

url.description: On the provider's own domain. The key goes there in the wire's usual header, and to nowhere else.

method.description: `GET`: a route that answers 2xx for a working key (an account or key page). `POST`: a route that checks the key before it reads the request; it is sent an empty JSON object, so a working key is turned down only for the empty request (2xx, 400 or 422) and nothing runs.

check.description: The provider's own route that refuses a wrong key with 401 or 403, asked before the model list when the list cannot tell a wrong key (it is open to anyone, or it is not a list). An answer that says neither (a 404, a 5xx) falls back to the model list.

env.description: The variable that overrides the address for the engine.

editable.description: The person may change the address (a server on this computer, an endpoint of your own).

pin.description: boopis always sets the address to `default`, so the engine does not choose another by itself (it would otherwise follow a coding-plan key to a coding-plan endpoint).

method.description: `engine_options`: the engine's own model listing for the slug. `get_models`: GET `path` (then `fallback_path`) on the base URL. `probe`: a loopback probe (`host`, `port`, `path`, `shape`), run only when Settings > Models opens and on Check again. `none`: nothing to list.

shape.description: What the answer must look like to count as that runtime (anything else, such as an HTML page, is not it).

flow.description: `cli`: the user's own program signs in, run from the host's login table. `cli_drive`: the engine drives the user's own program, which holds the login. `device_code`: a flow the host owns, tokens in the keychain. `official_program`: the host owns the flow of a lab's program for open-source apps (ChatGPT). `external_token`: a token file the engine reads (hidden).

owner.description: The code that owns the sign-in (claude.rs, chatgpt/).

kind.description: `terms`: what the lab's terms allow, which the owner approves. `limit`: a plan or quota limit. `info`: anything else a person should know.

where.description: `row`: shown under the row itself. `detail`: shown in the card that opens from the row.

heavy.description: One heavy-model switch (ADR-0037, ADR-0039): what `setup_set_heavy(id, on)` takes. Replaces the host's hard-coded table; nothing in the host branches on an id.

id.description: Also the tier's name on the ladder.

reason.description: Why it is off by default, from ADR-0037's figures only.

engines.description: The switch applies when every tier of the saved ladder is on one of these.

key_way.description: The key way whose key must be in place when no ladder is saved (and for the plugin's default ladder to stand).

applies_when_unset.description: Whether the switch also applies when no ladder is saved and `key_way`'s key is in place.

pick.description: `route_alias`: the Claude route's own alias or model. `lowest_in_family`: the lowest model of `family` the provider's catalogue lists.

not_applicable.description: The sentence for `hx.setup.subscription_unavailable` when it does not apply.

none_listed.description: The sentence when the catalogue lists no model of the family (for `lowest_in_family`).

empty_ladder.description: What to do when turning it off leaves a ladder with no tier: `unset` saves none (governed mode then says why); `keep` never leaves a ladder empty.

fields.description: The `endpoint` form's fields, in order. The builders on both sides turn each into a schema property (`secret` is `x-secret`, `multi` `x-multi`, `multiline` `x-multiline`, `mono` `x-mono`); `after_test` fields exist only once Test has found models.

waits_for.description: `owner`: a decision only the owner can make. `terms`: the lab's terms do not allow it. `later`: a later wave. `none`: not possible.

example.description: What a reader must answer for a way. `expect` maps a dotted path (`key.wire_var`, `discovery.port`) to its value; `shown` is the entry's, `secret_ref` is `secret://provider.<engine or slug>/api_key` (null for a way with no key), the rest are the way's own fields.
